title: A Landfall for the Passage
premise: Sable Delacroix has spent a decade outrunning a past mistake by never staying anywhere longer than a season, flying supplies into remote river settlements. When dying prospector Elias Wren trades her a map to the forbidden headwaters of the Kestrel River in exchange for a promise to deliver it to his estranged daughter, Sable expects a simple errand. Instead, the map draws the attention of the Meridian Company, which will do anything to keep the river's source — and its mineral wealth — hidden, forcing Sable to team up with Wren's daughter, the stubborn cartographer Ines, and her old rival pilot Callum Reyes. As the dry season shrinks the river and the Company closes in, Sable must choose between the loyalty she owes the people who once covered for her crime and the truth that could finally let her stop running; in the end she exposes the Company's buried secret at the source, accepts the cost of her own past, and finds that belonging was something she had to land for, not fly toward.
about_author: Zephyrine Villalobos is the pen name of a former floatplane dispatcher who spent six years logging weather and river conditions along the northern interior before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people who mistake motion for freedom.

chapters.title: Fuel, Weather, Rumors
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A routine medicine run into the settlement of Halfway Bend establishes her world: the plane, the gossip she ferries alongside cargo, and her rule of never staying past a season. When a friend asks her to stay for the winter festival, she deflects. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as freedom.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wouldn't Die Quietly
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She finds prospector Elias Wren collapsed at a strip only she services. He offers her a hand-drawn map to the Kestrel headwaters if she'll carry it to his daughter in Port Anselm. Sable refuses at first — maps like this get pilots killed. Emotional beat: reluctant compassion overriding self-preservation.

chapters.title: A Promise Made at Altitude
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Wren dies before dawn, and Sable, honoring a promise made half to comfort him, takes the map. In his effects she finds a Company ledger page suggesting the headwaters are more than legend. Emotional beat: guilt as inheritance.

chapters.title: Port Anselm, Port of Lies
chapters.summary: Ines Wren's POV. Ines, a cartographer who has spent years mapping everything except her father's life, receives Sable coldly. She recognizes the map's handwriting but not its route. A Meridian Company surveyor begins asking pointed questions around town. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into suspicion.

chapters.title: Two Copies of Every Truth
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Comparing the map against her father's letters, Ines realizes he'd been searching the headwaters for twenty years — and that someone burned part of his records. She confronts Sable, who admits the ledger page exists but hides why she knows what the Company does to people who talk. Emotional beat: two liars recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Hangar Fire
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Someone torches the hangar where the Otter is parked; the map survives only because Sable slept beside it. The fire marshal calls it electrical. Both women know better. Ines insists on coming upstream; Sable says no. Emotional beat: fear hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Callum Reyes Lands Hard
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Rival pilot Callum Reyes arrives offering charter services — and quietly reports to the Meridian Company, who've promised him the routes Sable flies. But reading Wren's name in their files unsettles him; Wren once saved Callum's engine over the Kestrel rapids. Emotional beat: ambition meeting an unpaid debt.

chapters.title: Upstream Against the Season
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Outvoted, Sable flies Ines to the last navigable bend before the dry season strands them. The river is already dropping. They begin upstream by boat with a guide who abandons them at the first canyon. Emotional beat: commitment after the point of no return.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. In the canyon they find Wren's old camp: twenty years of journals revealing he wasn't prospecting — he was documenting a Company massacre at the source decades ago and hiding the evidence where only the river could guard it. Emotional beat: a father redeemed posthumously.

chapters.title: The Dry Season Closes Its Fist
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Rapids become gravel bars; the boat must be portaged. Sable confesses her past: she once flew Company muscle to a village that was then burned, and has run from that complicity ever since. Ines doesn't forgive her — but doesn't leave. Emotional beat: truth offered without guarantee of absolution.

chapters.title: Callum's Contrition
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Ordered to intercept them, Callum instead lands upstream and leaves fuel and food where they'll find it, tipping the Company off to nothing. His handler grows suspicious. Emotional beat: loyalty transferred from employer to conscience.

chapters.title: The Company Comes Upstream
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A Meridian expedition — armed, well-provisioned, led by the surveyor from Port Anselm — enters the canyon behind them. The women realize the Company isn't chasing a map; it's erasing witnesses, and Wren's evidence would end it. Emotional beat: being hunted changes the mission from discovery to survival.

chapters.title: Portage of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A grueling overland portage past a waterfall, carrying the boat and the journals. Ines sprains an ankle; Sable carries her gear and, in fragments, her father's story back to her. They stop being strangers. Emotional beat: intimacy forged by shared weight.

chapters.title: Radio Silence
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. The Company grounds Callum and confiscates his radio, planning to use his plane for the pursuit. He sabotages the fuel lines just enough to delay them a day, knowing it ends his career and maybe his life. Emotional beat: sacrifice without applause.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. They reach the headwaters: a spring-fed basin above a drowned valley, and beneath the waterline, the sealed Company cache — records, photographs, payrolls proving the massacre. The pursuers' boats appear below. Emotional beat: awe immediately curdled by dread.

chapters.title: Standoff at the Spring
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Cornered at the basin, Sable bargains with the surveyor while Ines dives for the cache. The surveyor reveals he knows exactly who Sable is — and offers her immunity in exchange for the evidence and silence. Her whole life of running distilled into one offer. Emotional beat: temptation at its most reasonable.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Weight You Choose
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines surfaces with the waterproof tin. Sable refuses the deal. The surveyor orders shots fired; Callum, having escaped and flown upriver on fumes, crash-lands between the parties, buying seconds with wreckage and nerve. Emotional beat: three loyalties colliding into one act of defiance.

chapters.title: The Long Glide Down
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. With the basin too enclosed for takeoff, Sable and Ines haul the tin downriver through the pursuers' line under cover of Callum's smoke, reaching the last stretch of deep water. Sable is grazed by a bullet. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into purpose.

chapters.title: Evidence Like a Flood
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. At Halfway Bend, the settlement that once sheltered Sable rallies: the medicine-run network becomes an evidence network, copying documents onto every plane heading out. The Company's story drowns under its own paper trail. Emotional beat: community as the thing Sable spent years refusing to see.

chapters.title: Reckoning
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. An inquiry convenes in Port Anselm. Sable testifies to both crimes — the Company's and her own — surrendering her license pending review. The surveyor and his superiors are indicted. Callum testifies too, ruining himself to finish what Wren started. Emotional beat: the cost of truth paid willingly.

chapters.title: Grounded
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Waiting out the license review, Sable stays in Halfway Bend through the first rains of the wet season — the longest she has ever stayed anywhere. She and Ines begin mapping the river properly, together, as a public record. Emotional beat: stillness chosen, not imposed.

chapters.title: A Landfall for the Passage
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Her license restored, Sable flies the first supply run of the new season — but now every flight ends with a landing somewhere she's expected. She scatters the last of Wren's ashes at the source on a detour home. Emotional beat: arrival, at last, as a way of living rather than an ending.
